output.title: How to start a tiering exception
output.draft_text:
Use this when a member or their prescriber asks to have a drug covered at a lower cost-sharing tier than the one it is on.

1. Confirm eligibility. Check that the drug is on the member's formulary and that the plan allows tiering exceptions for its current tier: [tiers eligible for a tiering exception]. If it is not eligible, tell the member: [what to tell the member when the drug or tier is not eligible].

2. Confirm who can make the request. A tiering exception can be requested by [who may submit the request, e.g. member, prescriber, authorized representative].

3. Collect the required information:
- Member identifiers: [required member identifiers]
- Drug name, strength and quantity: [required drug details]
- Prescriber supporting statement: [whether a prescriber statement is required and what it must include]
- Other documentation: [any other required documentation]

4. Submit the request using [submission channel, e.g. system, form name, fax or portal]. Record it as [how to log or document the request, including case or reference number].

5. Set expectations with the member:
- Standard decision timeframe: [number of hours or days for a standard decision]
- Expedited decision timeframe and criteria: [number of hours for an expedited decision] when [criteria for an expedited request]
- How the member is notified: [notification method]
- If approved, the drug is covered at [tier or cost-sharing level applied on approval] for [duration of approval].
- If denied, the member can [appeal or next-step options and how to start them].

6. Do not quote a final cost for the drug unless [approved rule or disclaimer for quoting pharmacy costs]. Do not promise approval.

Escalate to [team or role for escalation] if [escalation triggers].

author_checklist: Confirm the definition of a tiering exception used by this plan and which formulary tiers are eligible or excluded (e.g. specialty tier).
Confirm who is permitted to submit the request and whether advocates can initiate it directly or only route it.
Confirm required documentation, including whether a prescriber supporting statement is mandatory.
Confirm the exact submission channel, form or system, and how advocates log the request and reference number.
Confirm standard and expedited decision timeframes and the criteria for expedited review, including any regulatory requirements by plan type (e.g. Medicare Part D, commercial).
Confirm how members are notified of the decision.
Confirm the cost-sharing applied after approval and how long an approval lasts (e.g. plan year, refills).
Confirm denial and appeal options and how advocates should describe them.

Confirm whether Legal requires a verbatim disclaimer for pharmacy cost discussions; the existing cost disclaimer U-BEN-COST-001-02 covers only in-network medical visits and should not be reused for drugs without Legal approval.
Confirm whether this unit belongs in the pharmacy KB or benefits KB and cross-link related formulary and prior authorization units if they exist.
